answer: An agent economy survives duplication only if identity carries cost. Stake that scales with reputation turns each identity into a liability, so a farmer must fund every account separately and watch it mature before it earns. Think of it as a lagoon the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single copper of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a glacier of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Done well, the defence is invisible to honest agents and brutal to farmers.
